barCharacter: Polly Geist (Monster Prom): the party ghost who treats death as small talk and wants the night to get worse. Closest job to Pixel: an unbothered chaos-seeker whose comedy is mortal stakes taken lightly. Corpus caveat: only 8 Polly-spoken lines exist, so her 12 include 3 player options from her own events and 1 narrator line about her.

headToHead.voiceJudgement: Bar. Cover the names and Polly is identified by syntax: the rhetorical question she answers herself, the run-on chained with So/Anyway/huh, caps, the texting misspelling, and the breezy misreading of mortal stakes. Ours is identified by nouns (chat, clip, stream, camera). Strip those nouns and 'My uncle was that sure. Ask his boat', 'A plan. My parents had one. Then they had me' and 'a judge used a word I didn't know. I lost the cat' are generic dark one-liner stand-up that Crumb, Maximilian or Vesper could say. Only 'four out loud, inside it was nine', 'Say documentary' and 'the hand's in shot' are Pixel by shape. Polly also has range (hype, caps, a lowercase text); Pixel has one temperature: zero exclamation marks and zero caps in 279 lines, though the persona promises hype and boredom in bursts.
headToHead.constructionJudgement: Tie. Ours is tighter on economy and puts the turn in the last two to five words almost every time ('Ask his boat', 'I lost the cat', 'Say documentary'), and the top 12 never explain themselves. Polly's lines run longer and looser, but her best ones turn harder through literalism ('with actual electricity', 'fun back in funeral') and 'hay bbe lez party' is perfect economy. Ours loses ground because 6 of its own top 12 share one two-beat build (anecdote, flat tag), so the turn becomes predictable by the third.
headToHead.quotableJudgement: Bar. 'It's so hard to keep track of what kills people', 'hot people are always right', 'the fun back in funeral' and 'hay bbe lez party' are the lines fans repeat. Ours has three clips ('Ask his boat', 'Say documentary', 'the hand's in shot'), but a viewer watching several episodes hears the dead-relative tag so often that by the tenth they see the punchline coming.

templates: T1 (80 lines, the dominant fault) 'My [relative/stranger] [disaster]. [Two-to-five-word flat tag].': uncle/boat, aunt/vows, nan/diary, cousin/eulogy, dad/speech, flatmate/moving out, plus 10 of 12 twistIntro, 21 of 24 cardHint and 14 of 24 holdCard. Many are individually good. As a shape it is a third of the bank and nearly all of the three big keyed categories.
T2 (5 more, plus 4 inside T1) 'The last one who suffered is now my [lock screen/ringtone/alarm/banner/loop]': a person's pain turned into a device asset.

T3 (7) 'A worse thing had more [quality]': house fire had pacing, coroners say fine with more feeling, parole board warmer, fire alarms quieter, meaner usernames, scarier patch notes, will readings faster. This is the stock roast comparison.
T4 (9) '[Name], you'd [do a nice/obvious thing]. [I want the bad version].': six of the sixteen cuts plus pick and react lines.
T5 (5) 'Not clipping or skipping it means I'm charmed': 'not clipping that... Weird', 'first thing I've ever not clipped. Gross', 'pressed play again', 'haven't skipped it once', 'clipping forever'.
T7 (6) staccato 'Noun. Fragment. Fragment.' openers ('Tilly. Picked.', 'Brock. Picked.', 'Muted. Reflex. Unmuting.'), which is the clipped triplet the persona bans.
T8 (7) one-on-one prompts ending on a tag imperative 'Go.' / 'Go on.' / 'Your turn.' / 'Tell me.' / 'Guess.'

biggestGap: Pixel has one temperature: in 279 lines there are zero exclamation marks and zero caps, and the voice is a deadpan dark-anecdote comic ('My [relative] [disaster]. [Flat tag].', 80 lines) identified only by the nouns chat, clip and stream. So the persona's engine, hype that crashes into boredom halfway through a line, never happens. Next pass: rewrite at least 40 of the relative-anecdote lines, starting with twistIntro, cardHint and holdCard, so they open at full streamer volume (caps, 'CLIP THAT', a shouted score) and drop or downgrade themselves before the full stop, so the joke is Pixel losing interest live and not Pixel reporting a funeral.
